title: 3.8.10 Lab: Round-Trip an Object Through JSON
description: Save an object to JSON text, restore it with JSON.parse, and prove the restored copy is independent of the original. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create an object
steps.instructions: Create a variable called player holding an object with at least two properties, one of them a number.

steps.title: Save it to text
steps.instructions: Use JSON.stringify to turn player into a string, and store that string in a variable called saved.

steps.title: Restore it
steps.instructions: Use JSON.parse on saved to build a variable called restored back into a usable object.

steps.title: Prove it works
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print a number property of the restored object plus one, and print one of the original properties. Confirm the restored value behaves like a real object.

requirements.title: Object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Declare player as an object in braces with at least two properties, one of them a number.

requirements.title: Saved with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify to produce text. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: JSON.stringify(player) turns the object into text. Keep that text in a variable.

requirements.title: Restored with parse
requirements.description: Calls JSON.parse on the saved text. Help: 3.8.8 (JSON.parse — Text Back to Object)
requirements.hint: JSON.parse(saved) turns the text back into an object. Keep it in a variable.

requirements.title: Both logged
requirements.description: Calls console.log to print the restored object. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Print a number from the restored object plus one, and print a property of the original.

requirements.title: restored is a separate object rebuilt from the saved text
requirements.description: saved is a string, and restored is a different object holding the same data as player. Help: 3.8.9 (Example: A Round Trip)
requirements.hint: Do the full trip: saved = JSON.stringify(player), then restored = JSON.parse(saved). Do not just assign restored = player.

checks.expr: typeof saved === 'string' && restored !== null && typeof restored === 'object' && JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(saved)) === JSON.stringify(player) && JSON.stringify(restored) === JSON.stringify(player) && Object.keys(player).length >= 2
checks.fail: saved should be the JSON text of player, and restored should be an object rebuilt from saved that holds the same data as player.
